newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Kerry Holdings to launch US$500 mln loan.
newsitem.headline: Kerry Holdings to launch US$500 mln loan.

text.p: Kerry Holdings plans to launch a US$500 million five-year unsecured syndicated loan facility, arrangers of the loan said on Friday.

Kerry Holdings is a member of Malaysian tycoon Robert Kuok's diversified group. It has substantial interests in major Hong Kong-listed companies, such as Kerry Properties, Shangri-La Asia and Television Broadcasts Ltd.
Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce, HSBC Investment Bank Asia and J.P. Morgan Securities Asia are coordinating arrangers.
A select number of relationship banks will also be invited as senior arrangers and arrangers to underwrite the facility together with the coordinating arrangers.
HSBC Investment Bank and J.P. Morgan Securities Asia will act as bookrunners, while Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce will act as agent for the facility.

Banks joining the facility may participate in either U.S. or Hong Kong dollars. The interest margin of the facility is 70 basis points per annum for U.S. dollars and 75 basis points per annum for Hong Kong dollars.
The facility is composed of two tranches.
The US$400 million tranche A is a straight term loan that will be used to refinance an outstanding US$400 million revolving credit dated December 18, 1995.
The US$100 million tranche B is a revolving credit for one year. Thereafter, the outstanding amount converts to a straight loan that repays at maturity.
Proceeds of the loan will be used for general corporate funding purposes of Kerry Holdings and its group companies.
